D24 — 2026-10-04
chose: D23's classifier as built, made strictly fail-safe. A command marks the session unless it is positively known to write nothing. It always marks on command or process substitution outside single quotes, and on output redirection to a file. Otherwise every segment must be one of these:
- a test run with no update flag (-u, --update…, --write);
- an allowlisted head that cannot write (cat, grep, rg, ls, wc, jq, echo, cd…);
- git with a working-tree-safe subcommand from an allowlist;
- sofar with a subcommand that writes only .sofar/;
- find with no delete or exec action, sed with no -i and no w or e command, sort or tree with no -o, or uniq with at most one operand.
Both engines assert one 99-command table.
over: D23 as first built. git was judged by a denylist (an unknown subcommand like `git lfs pull` skipped). `sofar`, `sort`, `uniq`, `tree`, `xxd` and `file` were allowed whatever their arguments (`sofar init`, `sort -o`, `uniq a b` write). Substitution (`echo $(rm x)`) and snapshot-updating test runs were not seen.
because: A missed write skips the gate, and the gate carries R4-A (D9). The orchestrator asked for an audit that every unrecognised command marks. The audit found these holes in the first build. A false mark costs one git spawn at Stop, about 20 ms; the D18 numbers are unchanged because the bench fixture's sessions carry no mark either way.
